newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher in all months.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Thursday, as the weaker yen against the dollar and the Chicago market's price gains overnight triggered active buying from individual investors, traders said.
Prices were 40 to 190 yen higher, with the benchmark January 1998 contract up 60 yen at 15,130 yen per tonne.
Individual investors actively bought from the opening, particulary in nearby months, traders said. In the afternoon, light technical selling capped the upside, they said.
"Some investors are shifting their money to volatile grain markets from the weaker precious metals," a trader said.
The spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was traded at $2.70-1/4 per bushel at 0835 GMT, against $2.70-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
The spot March soybean contract on the overnight trading system was at $7.39-3/4 a bushel, down from $7.40-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
